aspects.says: javac picks the attribute when it compiles the annotated class, and reflection also checks the annotation type's current retention, so a retention change needs every user recompiled.
basis: section:javac Applies Retention When It Compiles the Annotated Class, and Reflection Checks It Again

aspects.says: A CLASS annotation ships in the class file with its values, so only SOURCE keeps it out of the jar, and a tool that reads class files needs CLASS or RUNTIME.
basis: section:SOURCE Stops at the Compiler, CLASS Stops in the Class File, Only RUNTIME Reaches Reflection

aspects.says: An annotation type declared without @Retention is CLASS, so getAnnotation returns null for it, and asking the type for its @Retention returns null rather than CLASS.
basis: section:An Annotation Without @Retention Is CLASS, and Reflection Returns null for It

aspects.says: When a class named in an annotation element is missing, the annotation is returned and reading that element throws TypeNotPresentException.
basis: section:A RUNTIME Annotation Whose Class Is Missing at Run Time Disappears Without an Error

aspects.says: When an annotation's type is missing at run time, the class still loads and reflection silently leaves the annotation out; only code naming the type fails, with NoClassDefFoundError.
basis: section:A RUNTIME Annotation Whose Class Is Missing at Run Time Disappears Without an Error

aspects.says: An annotation processor sees annotations of every retention in the source it compiles.
basis: section:SOURCE Stops at the Compiler, CLASS Stops in the Class File, Only RUNTIME Reaches Reflection
aspects.reason: one clause pointing to unit 10.4.4, whose practices build and run processors

aspects.says: javac drops a SOURCE annotation, writes a CLASS annotation to RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations and a RUNTIME one to RuntimeVisibleAnnotations; only the last is returned by reflection.
basis: section:SOURCE Stops at the Compiler, CLASS Stops in the Class File, Only RUNTIME Reaches Reflection

aspects.says: Parameter and type-use annotations go to their own visible and invisible attributes, and a local variable's declaration annotation is never written.
aspects.reason: lookup table; the attributes behave like the method-level ones the practices check
